findings.sectionRef: US-004 / Acceptance Criteria — grep packages/ for retired symbols
findings.description: packages/happy-cli/src/daemon/daemon.integration.test.ts:20,143-160 still imports `encodeTunnelClaim` from `happy-server`, defines a local `TunnelClaimPayload` type, and mints a `tunnel <claim>` Authorization header via `mintTunnelAuth(..., accountId)`. The happy-server module no longer exports `encodeTunnelClaim` (US-002 deleted `tunnelClaim.ts` and the index re-export), so this test will fail to typecheck and fail at runtime. US-004's grep AC across `packages/` would catch this, but the iter-6 grep was scoped to `docs plans packages/*/CLAUDE.md` and missed the .ts file.
findings.resolution: F-001+F-002: Removed encodeTunnelClaim import + claim-minting helpers from daemon.integration.test.ts; replaced with makeFakeTunnelAuth() generating tunnel <uuid>. Deleted ambient encodeTunnelClaim export from happy-server.d.ts:77. Typecheck passes.
findings.suggestedFix: Either (a) rewrite the test to use `X-Tunnel-Authorization: tunnel <fake-jwt>` headers and drop the claim-minting helper entirely, mirroring how `socketTunnelAuth.test.ts` was rewritten in US-004, or (b) delete the test if its sole purpose was exercising the now-removed claim path. Also remove the matching `encodeTunnelClaim` declaration in `packages/happy-cli/src/types/happy-server.d.ts:77` and the local `TunnelClaimPayload` type in the test.

findings.description: packages/happy-cli/src/types/happy-server.d.ts:77 still declares `export function encodeTunnelClaim(payload: unknown, ed25519SecretKey: Uint8Array): Promise<string>;` as an ambient type for the `happy-server` module. The module no longer exports that symbol. Any consumer (currently daemon.integration.test.ts) that relies on this declaration believes the export exists. Even after the test is fixed, the stale ambient declaration must be removed so future code can't be written against a non-existent export.
findings.resolution: F-001+F-002: Removed encodeTunnelClaim import + claim-minting helpers from daemon.integration.test.ts; replaced with makeFakeTunnelAuth() generating tunnel <uuid>. Deleted ambient encodeTunnelClaim export from happy-server.d.ts:77. Typecheck passes.
findings.suggestedFix: Delete line 77 of the ambient `happy-server` module declaration.

findings.description: Two happy-app validation scripts still reference the retired tunnel-claim contract and the deleted file `packages/happy-server/sources/app/api/auth/tunnelClaim.ts`: (a) `packages/happy-app/scripts/check-sprint-a-gate.mjs:119-133` asserts `verifyTunnelClaim` is exported from `tunnelClaim.ts` and that the file does not import a JWT lib; that file no longer exists, so the gate check will throw at `readOrFail`. (b) `packages/happy-app/scripts/verify-refresh-supported.mjs:93-115,226-229` decodes a `tunnelClaim` envelope and requires `machines[0].tunnelClaim` from a `/pair/complete` response that no longer returns the field; the script will fail on every run. These scripts are no longer meaningful post-removal and the AC's `grep -rn 'tunnelClaim' packages/` would surface them.
findings.resolution: Rewrote check-sprint-a-gate.mjs and verify-refresh-supported.mjs to assert NEW contract (tunnel-claim artifacts absent). Deleted sprint-a-gap.md. Gate check 9/9 PASS; typecheck clean.
findings.suggestedFix: Delete both scripts (the Sprint A gate has been superseded by the claim removal) or rewrite them to assert the new contract: `verifyTunnelClaim` is absent, `tunnelClaim.ts` does not exist, and `/pair/complete` response shape no longer contains `tunnelClaim`. Also consider deleting/updating `packages/happy-app/scripts/sprint-a-gap.md` (descriptive doc referencing the retired layer) so it doesn't mislead future readers.

findings.description: packages/happy-app/sources/auth/tokenStorage.ts:40-55 `isAuthCredentials` is a structural type-guard that accepts any object with the known string/number fields but does not strip extra fields. A stale stored credential blob containing `tunnelClaim: '...'` will pass the guard, then `parseStoredCredentials` returns it unchanged, and the subsequent `updateMachineCredentials` (line 159-164) spreads the whole object back out via `{...machine, ...patch}`, re-persisting the retired field. This violates the plan's stated 'no NEW writes include the field' invariant for Group B. The on-disk credential is effectively immortal until the user re-pairs.
findings.resolution: Replaced isAuthCredentials guard with normalizeAuthCredentials projector; explicitly picks AuthCredentials fields and strips extras. Applied at parseStoredCredentials, setCredentials, updateMachineCredentials. 3 new tests verify field-stripping. All 14 tests pass.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the boolean type-guard with a `normalizeAuthCredentials(value: unknown): AuthCredentials | null` that explicitly picks only the known fields. Call it from `parseStoredCredentials` so stored blobs are sanitized on load, and from `setCredentials` / `updateMachineCredentials` so writes can never include leftover fields. Same field-allowlist projection on `writeStoredCredentials`.

findings.description: packages/happy-agent/src/auth.ts:160-201 spreads server-returned `primary` / `target.machines[0]` objects directly into the persisted `machines` array (`machines.push({ ...primary, tunnelId })` and `{ ...target.machines[0], tunnelId, connectToken, connectTokenExpiry }`). If a server still returns `tunnelClaim`, `accountId`, or any other retired field, those values are persisted into `credentials.json` and survive subsequent `loadCredentials` -> `saveCredentials` round-trips because `Credentials` is a `PersistedCredentials & {...}` intersection that doesn't field-allowlist. This is the same class of issue as F-004.
findings.resolution: Added toPersistedMachineCredentials projector in credentials.ts; applied at 5 machines.push() sites + loadCredentials. 4 new tests. Rebuilt dist/. 275 tests pass.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a `toPersistedMachineCredentials(input: unknown): PersistedMachineCredentials` projector that explicitly picks the documented `PersistedMachineCredentials` fields, and apply it before each `machines.push(...)` in `discoverAuthorizedMachines`. Optionally apply the same projection on read in `loadCredentials` so legacy on-disk files are sanitized.

findings.sectionRef: Out of Scope — unrelated test changes
findings.description: Two app tests changed in iter-3 (US-003) are out-of-scope for the tunnel-claim removal and weaken or shift coverage without a corresponding product change in this diff: `packages/happy-app/sources/components/AgentInput.activeRegression.test.tsx:169` flips an active-mode voice mic regression from `present` to `absent`, and `packages/happy-app/sources/sync/profile.test.ts:23` accepts an old local profile shape. Neither has anything to do with the claim header. The progress.txt iter-3 notes acknowledge this opportunistically ('Some broad app tests had stale expectations unrelated to the claim story').
findings.resolution: Kept both US-003 test changes (option a). AgentInput voice-mic: pre-US-003 toBeGreaterThan(0) was wrong — testId is not rendered. profile.test: ProfileSchema.safeParse accepts the local shape; pre-US-003 expected wrong throw. Added explanatory comments. 1056 tests pass.
findings.suggestedFix: Either (a) split these changes into a separate commit with explicit justification (so review can evaluate the coverage shift on its merits) or (b) revert them and let the failing tests motivate their own follow-up. Mixing them into the claim-removal landings makes per-story rollback less useful.

findings.description: The plan's last AC (line 146) requires a manual operator check that BOOX → daemon HTTP+socket succeeds without `X-Codexu-Authorization`, with the operator updating `docs/validation/devtunnels-boox-result.md` with a one-line confirmation. This is informational/operational rather than a code-review issue, but the diff updates `docs/validation/devtunnels-boox-result.md` (per progress.txt iter-6) without a fresh BOOX confirmation line dated post-implementation. Flag for operator follow-up before declaring the migration verified end-to-end.
findings.resolution: Added PENDING OPERATOR VERIFICATION blockquote under Phase 1 Notes in devtunnels-boox-result.md. Manual operator step still required pre-merge; placeholder prevents the doc from being mistaken for a post-implementation confirmation.
findings.suggestedFix: After this batch lands on `main`, run the BOOX tablet against the new server build and append a one-line confirmation entry (dated, with commit hash) to `docs/validation/devtunnels-boox-result.md`. Not blocking for merge, but blocking for closing the plan's manual-AC.
